'''Sergei Dmitriyevich Odintsov''' ({{langx|ru|Сергей Дмитриевич Одинцов}}; born 1959) is a Russian [[astrophysics|astrophysicist]] active in the fields of [[cosmology]], [[quantum field theory]] and [[quantum gravity]]. He received his master's degree and PhD in Physics at the [[Tomsk State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Odintsov |first=Sergei |title=Sergei D Odintsov Curriculum Vitae |url=https://api.icrea.cat/api/show-file/23655?token=e93QZVcbwi9MQxRz6wtTQzfAHr28aOEUdAPEPJfy2lA4d7E1KuZ61cSaXiLAPtqq}}</ref> Odintsov is an [[Catalan Institution for Research and Advanced Studies|ICREA]] Research Professor at the [[Institut de Ciències de l'Espai]] ([[Barcelona]]) since 2003. He also collaborates as group leader at research projects of the [[Tomsk State Pedagogical University]]. He is [[editor-in-chief]] of [[Symmetry (MDPI journal)|''Symmetry'']], and is a member of the [[editorial boards]] of ''[[Gravitation and Cosmology]]'',<ref>{{Cite web
 | title =Editorial Board of ''Gravitation and Cosmology''
 | publisher =Springer 
 | url =https://www.springer.com/physics/theoretical%2C+mathematical+%26+computational+physics/journal/12267?detailsPage=editorialBoard 
 | format =Online access 
 | access-date =2019-07-09}}</ref> ''[[International Journal of Geometric Methods in Modern Physics]]'',<ref>{{Cite web
 | title =Editorial Board of ''International Journal of Geometric Methods in Modern Physics''
 | publisher =[[World Scientific Publishing]] 
 | url =http://www.worldscientific.com/page/ijgmmp/editorial-board 
 | format =Online access 
 | access-date =2019-07-09}}</ref> ''[[International Journal of Modern Physics D]]'',<ref>{{Cite web
 | title =Editorial Board of ''International Journal of Modern Physics D''
 | publisher =[[World Scientific Publishing]] 
 | url =http://www.worldscientific.com/page/ijmpd/editorial-board 
 | format =Online access 
 | access-date =2019-07-09}}</ref> ''[[Journal of Gravity]]'',<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hindawi.com/journals/jgrav/editors/ |title=Journal of Gravity — an Open Access Journal |access-date=2014-06-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140707024635/http://www.hindawi.com/journals/jgrav/editors/ |archive-date=7 July 2014 }}</ref> [[Universe (journal)|''Universe'']],<ref name=edbo>
{{Cite web
 | title =Editorial Board of ''Universe''
 | publisher =MDPI Publishing

In 2011, Odintsov was included in the list of the top 10 most well-known scientists of Russian origin according to ''[[Forbes]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.forbes.ru/ekonomika-slideshow/lyudi/75452-10-samyh-izvestnyh-v-mire-uchenyh-russkogo-proishozhdeniya/slide/7 |title=10 самых известных в мире ученых русского происхождения. Сергей Одинцов &#124; Новости |access-date=2014-06-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140706105831/http://www.forbes.ru/ekonomika-slideshow/lyudi/75452-10-samyh-izvestnyh-v-mire-uchenyh-russkogo-proishozhdeniya/slide/7 |archive-date=6 July 2014 |date=20 October 2011 }}</ref> In 2014, he was included in the list of The World's Most Influential Scientific Minds: 2014 according to [[Thomson Reuters]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://thomsonreuters.com/articles/2014/worlds-most-influential-scientific-minds-2014 |title=The World's Most Influential Scientific Minds 2014 &#124; Thomson Reuters |access-date=2014-10-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141007000116/http://thomsonreuters.com/articles/2014/worlds-most-influential-scientific-minds-2014 |archive-date=7 October 2014 }}</ref> 

==Bibliography==
Odintsov has published 730 research articles with over 70.000 citations<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Odintsov, Sergei page at ICREA |url=https://www.icrea.cat/community/icreas/17422/sergey-odintsov/ |website=ICREA}}</ref> with an [[h-index|''h''-index]] of 127.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://inspirehep.net/search?ln=es&p=f+a+odintsov%2C+s+d&of=hcs&action_search=Buscar|title=Inspire}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=1j1w5V4AAAAJ|title=Sergei D. Odintsov}}</ref>

His main scientific results are in the fields of [[quantum field theory]] and [[quantum gravity]] and include the complete development of [[Quantum field theory in curved spacetime|renormalization group in curved space]], the discovery of [[asymptotic conformal invariance]], and a full description of curvature-induced phase transitions.<ref>Buchbinder, I. L., Odintsov, S. D., & Shapiro, I. L. (1992). Effective action in quantum gravity. (Tomsk Pedagogical Inst.) Published in Bristol, UK: IOP (1992) 413 p</ref> In [[cosmology]], together with [[Shin'ichi Nojiri]], Odintsov has proposed [[Brane cosmology|brane-world]] inflation (independently from the same proposal by [[Stephen Hawking]]).<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.62.064006|title=Quantum (in)stability of dilatonic AdS backgrounds and the holographic renormalization group with gravity|journal=Physical Review D|volume=62|issue=6|article-number=064006|year=2000|last1=Nojiri|first1=Shin'Ichi|last2=Odintsov|first2=Sergei D.|last3=Zerbini|first3=Sergio|arxiv=hep-th/0001192|bibcode=2000PhRvD..62f4006N|s2cid=15133708}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/S0370-2693(00)00629-8|title=Brane world inflation induced by quantum effects|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=484|issue=1–2|pages=119–123|year=2000|last1=Nojiri|first1=Shin'Ichi|last2=Odintsov|first2=Sergei D.|arxiv=hep-th/0004097|bibcode=2000PhLB..484..119N|s2cid=2379752}}</ref> In the study of [[dark energy|dark energy cosmology]], with [[Emilio Elizalde]] and [[Shin'ichi Nojiri]], Odintsov proposed a dark energy model consisting of complex scalar or two scalars (such model was later called [[Quintom scenario|quintom]]) with possibility to realize phantom or quintessence type of acceleration<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.70.043539|title=Late-time cosmology in a (phantom) scalar-tensor theory: Dark energy and the cosmic speed-up|journal=Physical Review D|volume=70|issue=4|article-number=043539|year=2004|last1=Elizalde|first1=Emilio|last2=Nojiri|first2=Shin'Ichi|last3=Odintsov|first3=Sergei D.|arxiv=hep-th/0405034|bibcode=2004PhRvD..70d3539E|s2cid=8695371}}</ref> as well as remove finite singularity there by quantum effects. Together with [[Shin'ichi Nojiri]], Odintsov also proposed a generalized [[Holographic principle|holographic dark energy]] model<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1007/s10714-006-0301-6|title=Unifying phantom inflation with late-time acceleration: Scalar phantom–non-phantom transition model and generalized holographic dark energy|journal=General Relativity and Gravitation|volume=38|issue=8|pages=1285–1304|year=2006|last1=Nojiri|first1=Shin'Ichi|last2=Odintsov|first2=Sergei D.|arxiv=hep-th/0506212|bibcode=2006GReGr..38.1285N|s2cid=119380235}}</ref> which includes eventually all possible variations over original holographic dark energy.

In 2002, [[Salvatore Capozziello]] proposed a fundamental new perspective of dark energy as caused by a modification of gravitational theory.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1142/S0218271802002025|title=Curvature Quintessence|journal=International Journal of Modern Physics D|volume=11|issue=4|pages=483–491|year=2002|last1=Capozziello|first1=Salvatore|arxiv=gr-qc/0201033|bibcode=2002IJMPD..11..483C|s2cid=7662085}}</ref> Based on this idea and further developing it, Odintsov and [[Shin'ichi Nojiri]] proposed the first unified picture for the evolution of the universe based on modified gravity.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.68.123512|title=Modified gravity with negative and positive powers of curvature: Unification of inflation and cosmic acceleration|journal=Physical Review D|volume=68|issue=12|article-number=123512|year=2003|last1=Nojiri|first1=Shin'Ichi|last2=Odintsov|first2=Sergei D.|arxiv=hep-th/0307288|bibcode=2003PhRvD..68l3512N|s2cid=8970997}}</ref> According to this, the evolution of the universe changes the gravitational theory, so that modified gravity changes the evolution of the universe making it to be accelerating at the very early and very late epochs. Later, they also demonstrated that such unified inflationary-dark energy universe may be achieved in modified [[Gauss-Bonnet gravity]]<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2005.10.010|title=Modified Gauss–Bonnet theory as gravitational alternative for dark energy|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=631|issue=1–2|pages=1–6|year=2005|last1=Nojiri|first1=Shin'Ichi|last2=Odintsov|first2=Sergei D.|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/875947|type=Submitted manuscript|arxiv=hep-th/0508049|bibcode=2005PhLB..631....1N|s2cid=119453685}}</ref> and non-local gravity.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2007.12.001|title=Modified non-local-''F''(''R'') gravity as the key for the inflation and dark energy|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=659|issue=4|pages=821–826|year=2008|last1=Nojiri|first1=Shin'Ichi|last2=Odintsov|first2=Sergei D.|bibcode=2008PhLB..659..821N|arxiv=0708.0924|s2cid=119273009}}</ref> This picture became even more popular recently due to the increasing possibility that [[Inflation (cosmology)|inflation]] is caused by modified gravity which differs from the usual [[general relativity]].
